Let me analyze this OIML certificate for a water meter.

Certificate details:
- Number: R49/2013-A-SK1-25.06
- Scheme: A
- Member State: SLOVAKIA
- Page total: 6
- Date issued: 23 January 2025 (from signature date "Date: 23th January 2025")
- OIML issuer ID: SK1 (from certificate number R49/2013-A-SK1-25.06)

Issuing authority:
- Name: Slovak Legal Metrology (SLM)
- Address: Geologická 9966/1, 821 06 Bratislava-Podunajské Biskupice, Slovakia; Product Certification Body, Hviezdoslavova 31, 974 01 Banská Bystrica, Slovakia
- Person responsible: Ing. Dušan Šmigura, PhD., Director of PCB
- oiml_issuer_id: SK1

Applicant:
- Spire Metering Technology LLC
- 34 Saint Martin Dr., Suite 13-A-9, Marlborough, MA 01752, USA

Manufacturer:
- Spire Metering Technology LLC
- 34 Saint Martin Dr., Suite 13 A-9, Marlborough, MA 01752, USA

Certified type:
- Category: "Water meter" — the schema lists examples; water meter fits. Category could be "Water meter".
- type_designations: ["280W-CI"]
- module_designation: "Ultrasonic water meter with electronic indication device"
- description: ultrasonic water meter description

Recommendation:
- id: R49 (canonical)
- edition: 2013
- scheme: A
- accuracy_classes: [1, 2] — wait, the certificate says "For accuracy class (if applicable): 1 and 2". But the technical table says "Accuracy class: 2". Hmm. The certificate attests conformity for accuracy classes 1 and 2. The table says Accuracy class 2. Should I include both? The recommendation.accuracy_classes should be [1, 2] per the certificate. Actually the type table says accuracy class 2. Hmm, but the certificate header says "For accuracy class (if applicable): 1 and 2". I'll use [1, 2] for recommendation.accuracy_classes since that's the conformity statement. Also record accuracy_class characteristic as 2 at type level? That's a conflict. Let me record recommendation accuracy_classes [1, 2], and characteristics type_level accuracy_class value 2? Actually the technical table shows accuracy class "2" — hmm wait, let me re-check: "Accuracy class | - | 2". Hmm, but the certificate says classes 1 and 2. Possibly the meter covers both class 1 and 2, but the data table states class 2. I'll record recommendation accuracy_classes as [1, 2] and type_level accuracy_class as 2 per the table. Actually to avoid conflict, maybe record the model-level accuracy? No — keep simple: recommendation.accuracy_classes [1,2], characteristics.type_level accuracy_class: 2. Hmm, but that might be inconsistent. Actually, wait — looking again: "Accuracy class | - | 2" — single value 2. But cover page says 1 and 2. I'll go with the cover page for recommendation, and table for type_level. Actually the R49 tables on page 4: "Accuracy class" value "2". Hmm.

Actually maybe better: type_level accuracy_class value "2" — but hold on, maybe it means the meter meets class 2 (and class 1 comes from the ratio R=250?). In R49, accuracy class is 1 or 2. The certificate says "For accuracy class: 1 and 2". The technical table says class 2. I'll keep both as extracted.

Test reports:
- OIML Type Evaluation Report No. 2025/ER043/SK1 dated 23 January 2025, 16 pages, role: type_evaluation_report
- Documentation file "Technical documentation file Spire Metering_280W-CI_00" dated 23 January 2025, 92 pages, role: documentation_file

Revision history:
- revision "0", date 2025-01-23, changes "Certificate first issued"

Dates: 23th January 2025 → 2025-01-23. date_issued: The certificate was issued... The revision table says certificate first issued 23 January 2025, and signature date is 23 January 2025. So date_issued: 2025-01-23.

Project number: "2025/ER043/SK1" — no, that's the report number. There's "FK-P05-85" form code and "V04/24-12-02" version. Project number isn't clearly stated. Omit.

Model family: The cert covers DN 50, 80, 100, 150, 200, 250 variants. These are size variants of the same type 280W-CI. Per the schema, include model_family only if cert covers >1 model variant. Here it covers 6 nominal diameter sizes. So models: DN=50, DN=80, DN=100, DN=150, DN=200, DN=250.

Model-level characteristics:
- nominal_dn: mm — 50, 80, 100, 150, 200, 250
- permanent_flowrate_q3: m³/h — 25, 63, 100, 160, 250, 400
- minimum_flowrate_q1: m³/h — 0.1, 0.252, 0.4, 0.64, 1, 1.6
- transitional_flowrate_q2: m³/h — 0.16, 0.4, 0.64, 1, 1.6, 2.56
- overload_flowrate_q4: m³/h — 31.25, 78.75, 125, 200, 312.5, 500
- construction_length: mm — 200, 225, 250, 300, 350, 450
- dimensions from Fig 1: width W: 175, 200, 220, 285, 340, 405; H1: 178, 203, 209, 245, 274, 300; H: 263, 292, 315, 383, 438, 480

Type-level characteristics:
- ratio_q3_q1: 250, unit R
- ratio_q2_q1: 1.6, dimensionless
- connection: "flange" (string value)
- installation_orientation: "H/V"
- water_temperature_range: {min: 0.1, max: 50}, unit °C; temperature_class: "T50"
- maximum_admissible_pressure: 16, bar
- pressure_loss: 0.16 bar? "Pressure loss class Δp: 0,16 bar / Δp 16" — value 0.16, unit bar, and pressure_loss_class: "Δp16". Hmm, "Δp 16" — pressure loss class. I'll record pressure_loss: 0.16 bar and pressure_loss_class: "Δp16".
- mpe_upper_flowrates: ±2% at water temp ≤30°C, ±3% at >30°C — this is config_level (temperature condition). Values: {condition: "water temperature ≤ 30 °C", value: 2, unit_symbol: "%"}, {condition: "water temperature > 30 °C", value: 3, unit_symbol: "%"}. The "Ø" is likely "θ" (water temperature). So condition axis: "water_temperature".
- mpe_lower_flowrates: ±5, unit %
- capacity_of_calculator: 9999999.99 m³
- capacity_of_calculator_high_resolution: 999.999999 m³ (0,999999 → "999,999999" → 999.999999)
- scale_interval: 0.01 m³
- scale_interval_high_resolution: 0.000001 L
- mechanical_class: "M1"
- climatic_class: "-55 to +85" °C → {min: -55, max: 85}, unit °C
- electromagnetic_class: "E1"
- environmental_class: "B / O" (climatic B / mechanical O)
- flow_profile_sensitivity_class: "U5D3"
- battery: non-replaceable li-battery 3.6 V, lifetime 10 years. Split: battery_voltage: 3.6 V; battery_type: "non-replaceable lithium"; battery_lifetime: 10 years.
- accuracy_class: 2

Matrix table: the dimensions table (Fig. 1) is a multi-dim table — capture as matrix_tables with columns type, dn, l, w, h1, h. Also the metrological table could be captured in matrix_tables too. I'll capture both:

matrix_tables:
1. name: "Technical and metrological data by nominal diameter", columns: [nominal_dn, permanent_flowrate_q3, minimum_flowrate_q1, transitional_flowrate_q2, overload_flowrate_q4, construction_length], rows per DN.
2. name: "Dimensions of the water meter type 280W-CI", columns: [type, dn, l, w, h1, h], rows per DN.

Components: The description mentions essential parts: flow sensor, calculator and indication device. I could record components:
- role: "flow sensor", type_designations: [] — description: iron cylindrical body with inlet and outlet firmly connected with plastic housing for the calculator. No type designations. characteristics maybe.
- role: "calculator and indication device": iron housing, PCB, measurement transducers (4 pcs), LCD 9 digits, lithium battery, red button.

The schema says include components only if cert names sub-assemblies. Here it does (flow sensor, calculator). I'll include with roles and descriptions in characteristics? characteristics{} is an object — I can include free-form entries. Let me be modest: components with role and characteristics like measurement_transducers_count: 4, display_digits: 9, display_range... Hmm, keep it light.

Software: software version 20.5.P.7, checksum 1202, display form "20.5.P.71202". Record in type_level: software_version: "20.5.P.7", software_checksum: 1202? Value 1202 could be number. Or string. Checksum as string "1202" is safer, but rules say numbers not strings. It's an identifier though, not a measured value. I'll put as string "1202" since it's a checksum (identifier). Actually rules: "Numbers, not strings." — for numeric values. Checksums are identifiers; string is fine.

Communication interfaces: M-Bus default; optional RS485 with MODBUS, pulse output, optical isolated, BACnet/MSTP, Radio, GSM. Record as type_level characteristic communication_interfaces: value ["M-Bus"]... values should be number|minmax|string. A list isn't specified. I could do optional_interfaces as a comma-joined string. Or omit. I'll add: communication_interface: {value: "M-Bus (default; optional: RS485 with MODBUS support, pulse output, optical isolated, BACnet/MSTP, radio, GSM)"}. Hmm, that's noisy. Maybe simpler: communication_interface: "M-Bus", optional_communication_interfaces: "RS485 (MODBUS), pulse output, optical isolated, BACnet/MSTP, radio, GSM". Fine.

Display: LCD 9 digits; indication range 999.999999 m³ to 9999999.99 m³. That matches calculator capacities. I'll skip display details in characteristics, or add display_digits: 9.

Installation orientation: H/V — horizontal and vertical. Value string "H/V".

MPE upper: "± 2 (at Ø ≤ 30°C) ± 3 (at Ø>30°C)" — Ø is likely θ (temperature). Config level:
attribute: "maximum_permisible_error_upper_zone" — hmm canonical: mpe_upper_flow_zone. axis: "water_temperature". values: [{condition: "θ ≤ 30 °C", value: -2..2?}] MPE ±2% → value could be 2 with note ±. I'll use value 2 and condition. Since MPE is ±, maybe value string "±2"? Rules say numbers. I'll use value 2, unit "%", and the attribute name mpe_upper_flow_zone implies ±. Fine.

mpe_lower_flow_zone: 5, "%".

Pressure loss: 0.16 bar and class "Δp16". Hmm wait — "Pressure loss class Δp: 0,16 bar / Δp 16". In R49, pressure-loss classes are Δp10, Δp16, Δp25, Δp40, Δp63, Δp100 (in units of 0.1 bar? Actually Δp63 = 0.63 bar). So Δp16 = 0.16 bar. Yes. Record pressure_loss: {value: 0.16, unit_symbol: "bar"}, pressure_loss_class: "Δp16".

Water temperature range: "0,1 to 50" °C → {min: 0.1, max: 50}. Temperature class T50.

Climatic class: -55 to +85 °C → {min: -55, max: 85}, unit °C.

Battery: 3.6 V ("below 3,6 V" in description, table says "3,6 V"). battery_voltage: 3.6 V. battery_lifetime: 10 years ("years" unit; unit_symbol "years"? unit_id null). battery_type: "non-replaceable lithium".

Scale interval: 0.01 m³; scale interval high resolution: 0.000001 L. Note "0,000001" → 0.000001.

Capacity of calculator: 9999999.99 m³ (display shows "9999999.99"). Capacity with high resolution: 999.999999 m³ ("999,999999").

Ratio Q3/Q1 = 250 (unit "R"). Ratio Q2/Q1 = 1.6.

Now model IDs: "DN50", "DN80", "DN100", "DN150", "DN200", "DN250". Attributes per model.

model_level entries:
- nominal_dn: values per model (unit mm)
- permanent_flowrate_q3
- minimum_flowrate_q1
- transitional_flowrate_q2
- overload_flowrate_q4
- construction_length (unit mm)
- overall_width_w, overall_height_h1, overall_height_h (mm) — from Fig 1. Actually "W" width, "H1", "H" heights. I'll name them dimension_w, dimension_h1, dimension_h. Or width/height_overall... I'll use "overall_width", "height_h1", "height_h". Canonical: width, h1, h? Let me use: dimension_w, dimension_h1, dimension_h. Hmm. The drawing labels are W, H1, H. I'll do width, height_h1, height_h. Actually simpler: "width", "height_h1", "height_h" with unit mm. Good.

Footnotes: none present. Skip footnotes array.

Certificate number: R49/2013-A-SK1-25.06. oiml_issuer_id: SK1.

Category: "Water meter".

Now let me also consider page_total: 6. project_number: omit or maybe "2025/ER043/SK1"? No, that's the TER number. Omit project_number.

Issuing authority address_lines: ["Geologická 9966/1", "821 06 Bratislava-Podunajské Biskupice, Slovakia", "Product Certification Body", "Hviezdoslavova 31", "974 01 Banská Bystrica, Slovakia"]. Person title: "Director of PCB". person_responsible: "Ing. Dušan Šmigura, PhD.".

Software table: put in matrix_tables? It's a 3-column table with one row. Could add to type_level characteristics. I'll do type_level: software_version "20.5.P.7", software_checksum "1202", software_display_format "20.5.P.71202".
